The original 24-module curriculum and four audits form a completed first edition. The website now continues with focused extensions authorized on 20 November 2026. New work should deepen a useful decision, connect to existing prerequisites and include inspected primary evidence, a concrete mechanism, counterexamples, separate worked practice and executed checks where appropriate.

How continued work is maintained

The website source repository is the working record for these additions. Existing first-edition exports and Library documents remain historical snapshots; this extension does not claim to update those downloads. Published lessons appear in search, topic browsing, study paths and progress tracking. Progress continues to be saved in your browser.

Keep the original R01–R24 identities stable. New extension sources use XR identifiers, with passage locators recorded below and in the relevant lesson. A future update should read this roadmap, inspect the repository’s actual state, finish one substantial item, validate it and publish to the same private site. Reconcile an existing partial lesson before creating another.

Extension evidence register

ID Primary source and inspected passages Use and limits
XR01 Nishtala et al., Scaling Memcache at Facebook, NSDI 2013, §3.2.1, printed p.388; inspected 2026-11-20 Historical lease-token mechanism; no current default or throughput prediction
XR02 RFC 9111, HTTP Caching, §§4.2–4.2.3, 4.4 and 6; inspected 2026-11-20 HTTP freshness/age and scope; application-cache example remains an original model
XR03 Marc Brooker, “Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter,” AWS Builders’ Library, “Retries and backoff” and final five paragraphs of “Jitter”; inspected 2026-11-20 Production experience with burst timing and retry guidance; X02 queue and deadline values are invented
XR04 Mike Ulrich, “Addressing Cascading Failures,” Google SRE, “Retries” and “Queue Management”; inspected 2026-11-20 Retry feedback, aggregate limits and waiting costs; no universal retry budget
XR05 Burton H. Bloom, “Space/Time Trade-offs in Hash Coding with Allowable Errors,” CACM 13(7), 1970, printed pp. 422–423 and 425–426, equations 16–17 and Table I; inspected 2026-11-20 Original one-sided membership model and analytical trade-off; deployment freshness is outside scope
XR06 Chang et al., “Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data,” OSDI 2006, §6 “Bloom filters,” proceedings p. 211 / PDF printed p. 7; inspected 2026-11-20 Deployed SSTable decision and qualitative disk-seek outcome; no universal percentage or sizing rule
XR07 Claude E. Shannon, “A Mathematical Theory of Communication,” Bell System Technical Journal 27, 1948, part I, §§1 and 6; inspected 2026-11-21 Entropy of a probability distribution; engineering hypothesis likelihoods remain model inputs
XR08 D. V. Lindley, “On a Measure of the Information Provided by an Experiment,” Annals of Mathematical Statistics 27(4), 1956, pp. 986–990, definitions 1–2; inspected 2026-11-21 Prior-to-posterior expected information and experimental-design framing; distinct from a specified loss function
XR09 OpenAI, GPT‑4 Technical Report, 2023, §3, §§3.1–3.2 and figures 1–3; inspected 2026-11-21 Small-run scaling evidence, registered predictions, observed success and exceptions; no claim that every capability scales predictably
XR10 Jacqueline Xu, Stripe, “Online migrations at scale”, “Why are migrations hard?”, “A pattern for online migrations,” parts 1–4 and Conclusion; inspected 2026-11-22 Production migration of hundreds of millions of live Subscription objects, staged decision and reported no-downtime outcome; no claim that dual writes are atomic
XR11 PostgreSQL 19 documentation, ALTER TABLE, ADD table_constraint [ NOT VALID ], VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, Notes and examples; inspected 2026-11-22 Current PostgreSQL constraint enforcement/validation and lock boundary; exact behavior remains version- and operation-specific
XR12 Shlomi Noach, GitHub, “gh-ost”, existing landscape, trigger limitations, Pauseable, operation modes and “gh-ost at GitHub”; inspected 2026-11-22 GitHub’s production MySQL constraint, triggerless/binlog choice and adoption; not a universal migration tool recommendation
XR13 Breck et al., “The ML Test Score,” IEEE Big Data 2017, Model 6, Infra 4 and 6–7, Monitor 2–7; inspected 2026-11-22 Production-readiness tests from experience and interviews across real ML systems; no universal metrics or release thresholds
XR14 Wang, Wang and Li, Uber, “Raising the Bar on ML Model Deployment Safety”, Introduction, safe deployment practices, Built for Adoption, Data Quality at Scale and Continuous Validation; inspected 2026-11-22 Uber’s 2025 scale, safeguards, adoption and reported detection improvement; transfer requires a local loss model and platform evidence
XR15 Rabanser, Günnemann and Lipton, “Failing Loudly,” NeurIPS 2019, Abstract, §3.1 and §5; inspected 2026-11-22 Empirical shift-detector comparison and documented representation/sample boundaries; not a universal detector or quality guarantee
XR16 GitLab, “Postmortem of database outage of January 31”, Timeline, Broken recovery procedures, Recovering GitLab.com, Root cause analysis and Improving recovery procedures; inspected 2026-11-23 Documents the 2017 failure, unavailable/missing recovery paths, six-hour snapshot choice, reported data loss, approximately 18-hour storage-bound restore and follow-up; not current GitLab architecture or a universal restore estimate
XR17 AWS Well-Architected, REL09-BP04, Desired outcome, Common anti-patterns and Implementation steps 1–7; AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Testing to achieve confidence, checks, considerations, drift and observability; inspected 2026-11-23 Current provider guidance on tested restore evidence, corruption cases and objective measurement; not proof that a configured workload meets its objectives
XR18 PostgreSQL 19 documentation, Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery, §§25.3.2–25.3.3 and 25.3.6; inspected 2026-11-23 Current base/incremental/WAL dependency and timeline semantics; deployed-version and tool behavior still requires local inspection
XR19 Uber, “Taming the ML Firehose: Scaling Feature Consistency”, Problem, Solution, Scale Challenges, Online Architecture Deep Dive, High Throughput and Conclusion; inspected 2026-11-24 Documents online/offline mismatches, exact inference-feature logging, scale constraints and reported rollout outcomes; no proof that logging is complete, unbiased or economical elsewhere
XR20 Nikhil Simha, Airbnb, “Chronon — A declarative feature Engineering framework”, entity sources, computation contexts/types and conclusion; Chronon Join documentation, timeline and accuracy scenarios; inspected 2026-11-24 Airbnb’s shared online/offline computation decision, temporal/snapshot semantics and reported adoption/productivity; source history and chosen accuracy mode remain local obligations
XR21 Feast, “Point-in-time joins”, full page, especially “Retrieving features as of the event time”; inspected 2026-11-24 Current event-time versus optional created-time filtering semantics; availability meaning and store support remain deployment inputs

Change record

24 November 2026 · Added X08 and five worked feature-time decisions. XR19 documents Uber’s feature mismatch, exact inference logging choice, scale constraints and reported rollout results; XR20 grounds Chronon’s shared temporal computation and accuracy modes; XR21 exposes the event-time versus availability-time boundary directly. Executed late-event, mutable-version, half-open-window and parity checks. Extension audit 03 is next.

23 November 2026 · Added X07 and five worked recovery decisions. XR16 documents GitLab’s 2017 recovery constraints, chosen six-hour snapshot, reported loss and approximately 18-hour storage bottleneck; XR17 bounds restore-test evidence; XR18 grounds PostgreSQL chain and timeline semantics. Executed recovery-point, dependency-path, incremental-closure and external-effect reconciliation checks. X08 is next, followed by extension audit 03.

23 November 2026 · Completed Extension audit 02. Re-inspected XR10–XR15 boundaries, verified 10 practice-to-answer mappings, executed both companion checks and checked generated routes, fragments, search and navigation. No lesson claim required correction. Selected X07 and X08 only for the concrete disaster-restore and point-in-time feature gaps recorded in the audit; audit 03 follows that mini-batch.

22 November 2026 · Added X06 and five worked AI release decisions. XR13 grounds slice, canary, rollback and continuous-monitoring controls; XR14 documents Uber’s platform decision and reported operational outcomes; XR15 bounds what distribution-shift detection establishes. Executed aggregate/slice, shadow-stratum, exposure-budget and delayed-label checks. Extension audit 02 is next.

22 November 2026 · Added X05 and five worked migration decisions. XR10 documents Stripe’s online Subscription migration; XR11 bounds PostgreSQL constraint enforcement and validation; XR12 documents GitHub’s lock-related migration problems and pauseable binlog-driven response. Executed stale-backfill, conflict, capacity and compatibility checks. X06 is next, followed by extension audit 02.

21 November 2026 · Completed Extension audit 01. Re-inspected XR01–XR09 boundaries, verified 20 practice-to-answer mappings, executed all four companion Python checks and checked generated routes, fragments, search and navigation. No lesson claim required correction. Selected X05 and X06 only for the concrete mutation-safety and AI-release gaps recorded in the audit; audit 02 follows that mini-batch.

21 November 2026 · Added X04 and five worked analyses. XR07–XR08 ground entropy and expected information; XR09 documents GPT‑4 small-run scaling predictions, their compute gap and reported exceptions. Checked all posterior, information-gain, decision-loss and cost-efficiency calculations. The X01–X04 extension audit is next.

20 November 2026 · Added X03 and five worked analyses. XR05 is Bloom’s original one-sided membership construction and trade-off; XR06 is Google’s Bigtable account of using filters to avoid SSTable disk seeks. Checked the sizing, expected-load, incremental-memory and version-mismatch examples. X04 is next.

20 November 2026 · Added X02 and four worked analyses. XR03 is Marc Brooker’s AWS Builders’ Library account of burst timing on EBS and Lambda. XR04 is Google SRE chapter 22 on retry feedback. The lesson records passage locators. Checked the synthetic queue, deadline and attempt calculations. X03 is next.

20 November 2026: X01 and its six worked analyses added, with an interactive comparison of unguarded and guarded cache fills. Executed ten legal schedules plus negative-premise fixtures, TTL boundary checks and exact load arithmetic. Original 24 modules retained. Real cache recovery, invalidation delivery and replica lag remain implementation questions; learner mastery is unknown. Next substantial item: X02.
